sanskrit: mahataś cāpy ahaṃkāra utpadyati narādhipa dvitīyaṃ sargam ity āhur etad buddhyātmakaṃ smṛtam
english: From the Great Principle, O lord of men, arises the I-sense; this they call the second creation, and it is remembered as having the nature of intellect.

sanskrit: ahaṃkārāc ca saṃbhūtaṃ mano bhūtaguṇātmakam tṛtīyaḥ sarga ity eṣa āhaṃkārika ucyate
english: From the I-sense comes into being the mind, whose nature is the qualities of the elements; this third creation is called that which springs from the I-sense.

sanskrit: manasas tu samudbhūtā mahābhūtā narādhipa caturthaṃ sargam ity etan mānasaṃ paricakṣate
english: From the mind, O lord of men, arise the great elements; this fourth creation they designate as the mental one.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhas tathaiva ca pañcamaṃ sargam ity āhur bhautikaṃ bhūtacintakāḥ
english: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as well — this the contemplators of the elements call the fifth creation, the elemental one.

sanskrit: śrotraṃ tvak caiva cakṣuś ca jihvā ghrāṇaṃ ca pañcamam sargaṃ tu ṣaṣṭham ity āhur bahucintātmakaṃ smṛtam
english: Ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose as the fifth — this they call the sixth creation, remembered as the seat of manifold reflection.

sanskrit: adhaḥ śrotrendriyagrāma utpadyati narādhipa saptamaṃ sargam ity āhur etad aindriyakaṃ smṛtam
english: Below arises the host of organs of action, O lord of men; this they call the seventh creation, remembered as that pertaining to the lower organs.

sanskrit: ūrdhvasrotas tathā tiryag utpadyati narādhipa aṣṭamaṃ sargam ity āhur etad ārjavakaṃ budhāḥ
english: The upward-flowing and the crosswise-flowing then arise, O lord of men; this the wise call the eighth creation, the natural one.

sanskrit: tiryak srotas tv adhaḥsrota utpadyati narādhipa navamaṃ sargam ity āhur etad ārjavakaṃ budhāḥ
english: The crosswise-flowing and the downward-flowing then arise, O lord of men; this the wise call the ninth creation, the natural one.

sanskrit: etāni nava sargāṇi tattvāni ca narādhipa caturviṃśatir uktāni yathāśruti nidarśanāt
english: These nine creations, and the four-and-twenty principles, O lord of men, have been declared according to scripture and tradition.

sanskrit: ata ūrdhvaṃ mahārāja guṇasyaitasya tattvataḥ mahātmabhir anuproktāṃ kālasaṃkhyāṃ nibodha me
english: Now hereafter, O great king, learn from me, in truth, the reckoning of time for this quality, as it has been declared by the great-souled ones.

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca avyaktasya naraśreṣṭha kālasaṃkhyāṃ nibodha me pañca kalpasahasrāṇi dviguṇāny ahar ucyate
english: Yājñavalkya said: Learn from me, O best of men, the reckoning of time for the Unmanifest. Five thousand kalpas, doubled, are called its day.

sanskrit: rātrir etāvatī cāsya pratibuddho narādhipa sṛjaty oṣadhim evāgre jīvanaṃ sarvadehinām
english: Its night, too, is of the same length, O lord of men; and when awakened, it first creates the herbs, the sustenance of all embodied beings.

sanskrit: tato brahmāṇam asṛjad dhairaṇyāṇḍasamudbhavam sā mūrtiḥ sarvabhūtānām ity evam anuśuśruma
english: Then it created Brahmā, born from the golden egg; that form is the embodiment of all beings — thus have we heard.

sanskrit: saṃvatsaram uṣitvāṇḍe niṣkramya ca mahāmuniḥ saṃdadhe 'rdhaṃ mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ divam ardhaṃ prajāpatiḥ
english: Having dwelt a year within the egg and come forth, the great sage, the Prajāpati, formed of half the whole earth and of half the heaven.

sanskrit: dyāvāpṛthivyor ity eṣa rājan vedeṣu paṭhyate tayoḥ śakalayor madhyam ākāśam akarot prabhuḥ
english: This is recited in the Vedas, O king, concerning heaven and earth; and between those two halves the Lord made the sky.

sanskrit: etasyāpi ca saṃkhyānaṃ vedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ daśa kalpasahasrāṇi pādonāny ahar ucyate rātrim etāvatīṃ cāsya prāhur adhyātmacintakāḥ
english: And for this one too the reckoning, declared by those versed in the Vedas and their auxiliaries, is: ten thousand kalpas less a quarter are called its day; and the contemplators of the inner self declare its night to be of the same length.

sanskrit: sṛjaty ahaṃkāram ṛṣir bhūtaṃ divyātmakaṃ tathā caturaś cāparān putrān dehāt pūrvaṃ mahān ṛṣiḥ te vai pitṛbhyaḥ pitaraḥ śrūyante rājasattama
english: The sage creates the I-sense, a being of divine nature, and four other sons; before his body, the Great Sage. These, it is heard, are the fathers of the very forefathers, O best of kings.

sanskrit: devāḥ pitṝṇāṃ ca sutā devair lokāḥ samāvṛtāḥ carācarā naraśreṣṭha ity evam anuśuśruma
english: The gods are the sons of the forefathers, and by the gods the worlds, moving and unmoving, are pervaded, O best of men — thus have we heard.

sanskrit: parameṣṭhī tv ahaṃkāro 'sṛjad bhūtāni pañcadhā pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam
english: The I-sense, the supreme abode, created the elements in five ways: earth, air, sky, water, and light as the fifth.

sanskrit: etasyāpi niśām āhus tṛtīyam iha kurvataḥ pañca kalpasahasrāṇi tāvad evāhar ucyate
english: For this one too, while it performs the third stage, they declare its night to be five thousand kalpas, and its day is said to be just as long.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaś ca pañcamaḥ ete viśeṣā rājendra mahābhūteṣu pañcasu yair āviṣṭāni bhūtāni ahany ahani pārthiva
english: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as the fifth — these are the particular qualities, O king of kings, in the five great elements, by which beings are pervaded day after day, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ spṛhayanty ete anyonyasya hite ratāḥ anyonyam abhimanyante anyonyaspardhinas tathā
english: These long for one another, delight in one another's welfare, esteem one another, and likewise contend with one another.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā anyonyaṃ guṇair hāribhir avyayāḥ ihaiva parivartante tiryagyonipraveśinaḥ
english: Slain by one another through their alluring qualities, yet imperishable, they revolve here in this very world, entering the wombs of beasts.

sanskrit: trīṇi kalpasahasrāṇi eteṣām ahar ucyate ratrir etāvatī caiva manasaś ca narādhipa
english: Three thousand kalpas are called the day of these, and the night is of the same length — and so too for the mind, O lord of men.

sanskrit: manaś carati rājendra caritaṃ sarvam indriyaiḥ na cendriyāṇi paśyanti mana evātra paśyati
english: The mind ranges, O king of kings, over all that is experienced by the senses; yet the senses do not see — here it is the mind alone that sees.

sanskrit: cakṣuḥ paśyati rūpāṇi manasā tu na cakṣuṣā manasi vyākule cakṣuḥ paśyann api na paśyati tathendriyāṇi sarvāṇi paśyantīty abhicakṣate
english: The eye sees forms, but through the mind, not through the eye alone; when the mind is distracted, the eye, though looking, does not see. So it is said that all the senses perceive only thus.

sanskrit: manasy uparate rājann indriyoparamo bhavet na cendriyavyuparame manasy uparamo bhavet evaṃ manaḥpradhānāni indriyāṇi vibhāvayet
english: When the mind is stilled, O king, the senses too come to rest; but when the senses are stilled, the mind does not come to rest. Thus one should recognize that the senses have the mind as their chief.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ hi sarveṣām īśvaraṃ mana ucyate etad viśanti bhūtāni sarvāṇīha mahāyaśāḥ
english: For the mind is called the lord of all the senses; into it all beings here enter, O greatly renowned one.

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca tattvānāṃ sargasaṃkhyā ca kālasaṃkhyā tathaiva ca mayā proktānupūrvyeṇa saṃhāram api me śṛṇu
english: Yājñavalkya said: The reckoning of the creation of the principles, and likewise the reckoning of time, have been declared by me in order; now hear from me the dissolution as well.

sanskrit: yathā saṃharate jantūn sasarja ca punaḥ punaḥ anādinidhano brahmā nityaś cākṣara eva ca
english: How Brahmā — without beginning or end, eternal and imperishable — withdraws creatures and creates them again and again.

sanskrit: ahaḥkṣayam atho buddhvā niśi svapnamanās tathā codayām āsa bhagavān avyakto 'haṃkṛtaṃ naram
english: Then, perceiving the waning of his day, his mind turned to slumber as the night comes on, the blessed Unmanifest urged onward the I-sensed Person.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasrāṃśur avyaktenābhicoditaḥ kṛtvā dvādaśadhātmānam ādityo jvaladagnivat
english: Then the sun of a hundred thousand rays, urged on by the Unmanifest, made himself twelvefold, blazing like fire.

sanskrit: caturvidhaṃ prajājālaṃ nirdahaty āśu tejasā jarāyvaṇḍasvedajātam udbhijjaṃ ca narādhipa
english: Swiftly with his blaze he burns up the fourfold web of creatures — the womb-born, the egg-born, the sweat-born, and the sprout-born, O lord of men.

sanskrit: etad unmeṣamātreṇa viniṣṭaṃ sthāṇujaṅgamam kūrmapṛṣṭhasamā bhūmir bhavaty atha samantataḥ
english: In the mere twinkling of an eye, all that is fixed and moving is destroyed, and the earth becomes everywhere level like the back of a tortoise.

sanskrit: jagad dagdhvāmitabalaḥ kevalaṃ jagatīṃ tataḥ ambhasā balinā kṣipram āpūryata samantataḥ
english: Having burnt the world, he of boundless might leaves the earth alone; then swiftly it is filled on every side with mighty waters.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālāgnim āsādya tad ambho yāti saṃkṣayam vinaṣṭe 'mbhasi rājendra jājvalīty analo mahān
english: Then, encountering the fire of Time, that water passes to destruction; and when the water is gone, O king of kings, the great fire blazes forth.

sanskrit: tam aprameyo 'tibalaṃ jvalamānaṃ vibhāvasum ūṣmāṇaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ saptārciṣam athāñjasā
english: That immeasurable, exceedingly mighty, blazing fire, the warmth of all beings, the seven-flamed — straightway then,

sanskrit: bhakṣayām āsa balavān vāyur aṣṭātmako balī vicarann amitaprāṇas tiryag ūrdhvam adhas tathā
english: the mighty wind, eightfold and powerful, of boundless breath, ranging crosswise, upward, and downward, devoured it.

sanskrit: tam apratibalaṃ bhīmam ākāśaṃ grasate ''tmanā ākāśam apy atinadan mano grasati cārikam
english: That irresistible and terrible wind the sky swallows into itself; and roaring beyond the sky, the mind swallows up the ranging sky.

sanskrit: mano grasati sarvātmā so 'haṃkāraḥ prajāpatiḥ ahaṃkāraṃ mahān ātmā bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyavit
english: The I-sense, the Prajāpati, the Self of all, swallows the mind; and the Great Self, knower of past, present, and future, swallows the I-sense.

sanskrit: tam apy anupamātmānaṃ viśvaṃ śaṃbhuḥ prajāpatiḥ aṇimā laghimā prāptir īśāno jyotir avyayaḥ
english: And even that incomparable Self, the universe — Śambhu the Prajāpati, possessed of minuteness, lightness, and attainment, the Lord, the imperishable light —

sanskrit: sarvataḥpāṇipādāntaḥ sarvatokṣiśiromukhaḥ sarvataḥśrutimāṃl loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
english: with hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads, and faces on every side, with ears on every side, abides in the world, enveloping all.

sanskrit: hṛdayaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ parvaṇo 'ṅguṣṭhamātrakaḥ anugrasaty anantaṃ hi mahātmā viśvam īśvaraḥ
english: The heart of all beings, of the measure of a thumb at the joint, the infinite great-souled Lord swallows up the universe.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavat sarvam akṣayāvyayam avraṇam bhūtabhavyamanuṣyāṇāṃ sraṣṭāram anaghaṃ tathā
english: Then all became imperishable, undecaying, and flawless — the sinless creator of beings past, future, and present.

sanskrit: eṣo 'pyayas te rājendra yathāvat paribhāṣitaḥ adhyātmam adhibhūtaṃ ca adhidaivaṃ ca śrūyatām
english: This dissolution has been duly expounded to you, O king of kings; now let the relation to the self, to the elements, and to the deities be heard.

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca pādāv adhyātmam ity āhur brāhmaṇās tattvadarśinaḥ gantavyam adhibhūtaṃ ca viṣṇus tatrādhidaivatam
english: Yājñavalkya said: The feet, say the Brāhmaṇas who perceive the truth, are the inner principle; that which is to be traversed is the elemental aspect; and Viṣṇu is the presiding deity there.

sanskrit: pāyur adhyātmam ity āhur yathātattvārthadarśinaḥ visargam adhibhūtaṃ ca mitras tatrādhidaivatam
english: The organ of excretion, say those who see the true meaning, is the inner principle; voiding is the elemental aspect; and Mitra is the presiding deity there.

sanskrit: upastho 'dhyātmam ity āhur yathāyoganidarśanam adhibhūtaṃ tathānando daivataṃ ca prajāpatiḥ
english: The organ of generation, they say according to the teaching of yoga, is the inner principle; pleasure is the elemental aspect; and Prajāpati is the deity.

sanskrit: hastāv adhyātmam ity āhur yathāsāṃkhyanidarśanam kartavyam adhibhūtaṃ tu indras tatrādhidaivatam
english: The hands, they say according to the teaching of Sāṃkhya, are the inner principle; the deed to be done is the elemental aspect; and Indra is the presiding deity there.

sanskrit: vāg adhyātmam iti prāhur yathāśrutinidarśanam vaktavyam adhibhūtaṃ tu vahnis tatrādhidaivatam
english: Speech, they declare according to the teaching of scripture, is the inner principle; what is to be spoken is the elemental aspect; and Fire is the presiding deity there.

sanskrit: cakṣur adhyātmam ity āhur yathāśrutinidarśanam rūpam atrādhibhūtaṃ tu sūryas tatrādhidaivatam
english: The eye, they say according to the teaching of scripture, is the inner principle; form here is the elemental aspect; and Sūrya is the presiding deity there.

sanskrit: śrotram adhyātmam ity āhur yathāśrutinidarśanam śabdas tatrādhibhūtaṃ tu diśas tatrādhidaivatam
english: The ear, they say according to the teaching of scripture, is the inner principle; sound there is the elemental aspect; and the quarters of space are the presiding deity there.

sanskrit: jihvām adhyātmam ity āhur yathātattvanidarśanam rasa evādhibhūtaṃ tu āpas tatrādhidaivatam
english: The tongue, they say according to the teaching of the principles, is the inner principle; taste alone is the elemental aspect; and the Waters are the presiding deity there.

sanskrit: ghrāṇam adhyātmam ity āhur yathāśrutinidarśanam gandha evādhibhūtaṃ tu pṛthivī cādhidaivatam
english: The nose, they say according to the teaching of scripture, is the inner principle; smell alone is the elemental aspect; and Earth is the presiding deity.

sanskrit: tvag adhyātmam iti prāhus tattvabuddhiviśāradāḥ sparśa evādhibhūtaṃ tu pavanaś cādhidaivatam
english: The skin, declare those skilled in the discernment of the principles, is the inner principle; touch alone is the elemental aspect; and the Wind is the presiding deity.

sanskrit: mano 'dhyātmam iti prāhur yathāśrutinidarśanam mantavyam adhibhūtaṃ tu candramāś cādhidaivatam
english: The mind, they declare according to the teaching of scripture, is the inner principle; what is to be thought is the elemental aspect; and the Moon is the presiding deity.

sanskrit: ahaṃkārikam adhyātmam āhus tattvanidarśanam abhimāno 'dhibhūtaṃ tu bhavas tatrādhidaivatam
english: That which springs from the I-sense, they say according to the teaching of the principles, is the inner principle; self-conceit is the elemental aspect; and Bhava is the presiding deity there.

sanskrit: buddhir adhyātmam ity āhur yathāvedanidarśanam boddhavyam adhibhūtaṃ tu kṣetrajño 'trādhidaivatam
english: The intellect, they say according to the teaching of the Veda, is the inner principle; what is to be known is the elemental aspect; and the Knower of the Field is the presiding deity here.

sanskrit: eṣā te vyaktato rājan vibhūtir anuvarṇitā ādau madhye tathā cānte yathātattvena tattvavit
english: This manifest power has been described to you in due order, O king, at the beginning, the middle, and the end, in truth, by one who knows the truth.

sanskrit: prakṛtir guṇān vikurute svacchandenātmakāmyayā krīḍārthaṃ tu mahārāja śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Nature transforms the qualities by her own will, of her own desire, for the sake of play, O great king, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: yathā dīpasahasrāṇi dīpān martyāḥ prakurvate prakṛtis tathā vikurute puruṣasya guṇān bahūn
english: As mortals kindle thousands of lamps from a single lamp, so Nature transforms the many qualities of the Person.

sanskrit: sattvam ānanda udrekaḥ prītiḥ prākāśyam eva ca sukhaṃ śuddhitvam ārogyaṃ saṃtoṣaḥ śraddadhānatā
english: Goodness, delight, abundance, gladness, and luminosity; happiness, purity, health, contentment, and faithfulness;

sanskrit: akārpaṇyam asaṃrambhaḥ kṣamā dhṛtir ahiṃsatā samatā satyam ānṛṇyaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīr acāpalam
english: freedom from meanness, absence of agitation, forbearance, firmness, harmlessness, evenness, truth, freedom from debt, gentleness, modesty, and steadiness;

sanskrit: śaucam ārjavam ācāram alaulyaṃ hṛdyasaṃbhramaḥ iṣṭāniṣṭaviyogānāṃ kṛtānām avikatthanam
english: purity, uprightness, good conduct, freedom from greed, absence of inner turmoil, and not boasting of deeds done amid the partings from the loved and the unloved;

sanskrit: dānena cānugrahaṇam aspṛhārthe parārthatā sarvabhūtadayā caiva sattvasyaite guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: showing favor through giving, working for another's good without craving gain, and compassion for all beings — these are remembered as the qualities of goodness.

sanskrit: rajoguṇānāṃ saṃghāto rūpam aiśvaryavigrahe atyāśitvam akāruṇyaṃ sukhaduḥkhopasevanam
english: The mass of the qualities of passion: form embodied in dominion, excessive eating, mercilessness, and the pursuit of pleasure and pain;

sanskrit: parāpavādeṣu ratir vivādānāṃ ca sevanam ahaṃkāras tv asatkāraś cintā vairopasevanam
english: delight in reviling others and the practice of quarrels, egotism, discourtesy, anxiety, and the cultivation of enmity;

sanskrit: paritāpo 'paharaṇaṃ hrīnāśo 'nārjavaṃ tathā bhedaḥ paruṣatā caiva kāmakrodhau madas tathā darpo dveṣo 'tivādaś ca ete proktā rajoguṇāḥ
english: torment, plundering, loss of shame, and crookedness; division, harshness, lust and anger, intoxication, pride, hatred, and abusive speech — these are declared to be the qualities of passion.

sanskrit: tāmasānāṃ tu saṃghātaṃ pravakṣyāmy upadhāryatām moho 'prakāśas tāmisram andhatāmisrasaṃjñitam
english: Now I shall declare the mass of those belonging to darkness; let it be marked: delusion, obscurity, gloom, and that known as blinding gloom;

sanskrit: maraṇaṃ cāndhatāmisraṃ tāmisraṃ krodha ucyate tamaso lakṣaṇānīha bhakṣāṇām abhirocanam
english: death is called blinding gloom, and anger is called gloom. Here are the marks of darkness: a craving for things to be eaten;

sanskrit: bhojanānām aparyāptis tathā peyeṣv atṛptatā gandhavāso vihāreṣu śayaneṣv āsaneṣu ca
english: insatiability in food and likewise no satisfaction in drink; indulgence in perfumes and garments, in amusements, in beds and seats;

sanskrit: divāsvapne vivāde ca pramādeṣu ca vai ratiḥ nṛtyavāditragītānām ajñānāc chraddadhānatā dveṣo dharmaviśeṣāṇām ete vai tāmasā guṇāḥ
english: delight in sleeping by day, in dispute, and in heedlessness; faith placed in dancing, instruments, and song through ignorance; and hatred of the particular duties of dharma — these are the qualities of darkness.

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca ete pradhānasya guṇās trayaḥ puruṣasattama kṛtsnasya caiva jagatas tiṣṭhanty anapagāḥ sadā
english: Yājñavalkya said: These three are the qualities of Primal Nature, O best of men; and they abide ever inseparable from the whole world.

sanskrit: śatadhā sahasradhā caiva tathā śatasahasradhā koṭiśaś ca karoty eṣa pratyagātmānam ātmanā
english: A hundredfold, a thousandfold, and likewise a hundred-thousandfold, and by tens of millions, this one makes the indwelling self by the self.

sanskrit: sāttvikasyottamaṃ sthānaṃ rājasasyeha madhyamam tāmasasyādhamaṃ sthānaṃ prāhur adhyātmacintakāḥ
english: The contemplators of the inner self declare that for the man of goodness the highest station, for the man of passion the middle, and for the man of darkness the lowest station.

sanskrit: kevaleneha puṇyena gatim ūrdhvām avāpnuyāt puṇyapāpena mānuṣyam adharmeṇāpy adhogatim
english: By merit alone here one attains the upward course; by merit mixed with sin, the human state; and by unrighteousness, the downward course.

sanskrit: dvaṃdvam eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ tu saṃnipātaṃ ca tattvataḥ sattvasya rajasaś caiva tamasaś ca śṛṇuṣva me
english: Now hear from me in truth the pairing of these three and their commingling — of goodness, of passion, and of darkness.

sanskrit: sattvasya tu rajo dṛṣṭaṃ rajasaś ca tamas tathā tamasaś ca tathā sattvaṃ sattvasyāvyaktam eva ca
english: In goodness passion is seen, and in passion likewise darkness; in darkness, too, goodness; and in goodness, the Unmanifest itself.

sanskrit: avyaktasattvasaṃyukto devalokam avāpnuyāt rajaḥsattvasamāyukto manuṣyeṣūpapadyate
english: He who is joined with the Unmanifest and goodness attains the world of the gods; he who is joined with passion and goodness is born among men.

sanskrit: rajastamobhyāṃ saṃyuktas tiryagyoniṣu jāyate rajastāmasasattvaiś ca yukto mānuṣyam āpnuyāt
english: He who is joined with passion and darkness is born in the wombs of beasts; and he who is joined with passion, darkness, and goodness attains the human state.
